title.narrative: Nigeria Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Scale-up Project

description.narrative: Operation Abstract: Summary Description of Proposed OperationNigeria DARES is envisioned as a scalable platform for achieving universal electrification and supporting energy transition through private sector investment. The platform aims to provide – (i) basic electrification (multiple lighting, radio, and mobile phone charging ability) to over 13 million unserved, rural, and remote Nigerians through the deployment of standalone solar, and (ii) grid equivalent electrification via mini grid to over 2.7 million Nigerians, in rural and peri urban settings. The platform will also support Nigeria's clean energy transition by increasing the reliability of electricity supply for 1.3 million existing electricity consumers, in peri urban and urban areas, by connecting them to cleaner and more reliable interconnected mini grids that will help replace approximately 288,000 diesel/gasoline gensets. The platform will also support the electrification of federal and state public institutions, such as healthcare and educational facilities, with distributed renewable energy (DRE) under an energy-as-a-service business model to crowd in private sector investment and ensure sustainable operation and maintenance (O&M). The platform will also provide an estimated 237,000 micro, small and medium enterprises (including around 124,000 agri-businesses) with reliable and clean electricity for productive uses that will help improve their economic output, create local jobs, and improve the financial sustainability of mini grids. The focus of the program is on scaling up mini grids and SAS deployment in Nigeria.The project supports the following components:Component 1. Solar Hybrid Mini Grids for Economic Development will support the development of privately owned and operated solar hybrid mini grids in unserved (primarily rural and remote) and underserved (primarily urban and peri-urban) areas that have high economic growth potential. It will also support the electrification of public institutions at the federal and sub-national level such as healthcare and educational facilities. The mini grid component consists of two investment sub-components defined by the different approaches they follow and will be implemented in parallel: Sub-component 1.1- the minimum subsidy tender and sub-component 1.2- performance-based grant program.Component 2: Standalone Solar Systems (SAS) for Households, MSMEs, and agribusinesses will expand availability and affordability of standalone solar systems (SAS) for households, MSMEs, and agribusinesses in rural areas. Through targeted and competitively awarded performance based grants, the uptake of 2,750,000 quality-certified solar home systems (SHS) and 75,000 PUE products in rural areas and amongst lower income segments will be promoted. Furthermore, solar solutions will be provided under an energy-as-a-service business model targeting MSMEs, economic clusters such as markets, plazas, trading centres, and agro-processing zones. Under the component, the Performance Based Grants (PBG) will provide results-based payments per connection. Component 3. Technical Assistance will support the creation of a framework for rural electrification upscaling, support project implementation, as well as broad capacity building at REA, NERC, FMPWH and other relevant stakeholders. It includes three sub-components: Institutional Strengthening and Policy Reform, Supporting DARES Ecosystem and Implementation, and Supporting States to Develop Solar Rooftop Ecosystem
The project development objective (PDO) is to increase access to electricity services for households, public institutions and MSMEs with private sector led distributed renewable energy generation.

baseline.value: Insufficient regulatory framework for mini grids in place.

target.value: Improved regulatory framework for mini grids is in place.

actual.value: The Nigeria Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) is currently reviewing key considerations that necessitates the upward review of the capacity of mini-grid projects to above 1MW. These considerations cuts across financial, process, technical, and environmental and social compliance aspect of renewable energy generation development. Dialogue and stakeholder engagement is in progress

title.narrative: Presidential approval for a national electrification strategy and implementation plan (NESIP)

baseline.value: No National electrification strategy and implementation plan

target.value: National electrification strategy and implementation plan prepared by FMoP and REA in consultation with States and approved by the President

actual.value: Procurement of consultant to assist REA in the preparation of the National Electrification Strategy and Implementation Plan (NESIP) is about been concluded and engagement scheduled to commence in November 2024. Other stakeholder consultation including engagement with sub-national entities and state governors is on-going
